classification.difficultyReason: Reuses the supplied mast height across explicitly named right triangles, selects the appropriate trigonometric ratio, and rearranges tangent when the unknown is the denominator. Pythagoras is prescribed and the final sum is specified.

content.prompt: Students at an adventure camp erect a vertical mast $AB$, as shown in the diagram. $BC$, $BD$ and $BE$ are straight wires that are fixed to the ground at $C$, $D$ and $E$ respectively.

spec.description: Unshaded perspective diagram with B vertically above A, E left, C upper right and D lower right. Solid mast and wires; dashed red ground connections. Coordinates establish the schematic view only and are not measurements.
spec.mathematics: Solid segments AB, BE, BC and BD; dashed ground segments AE, AC and AD; labels A, B, C, D and E. No printed dimensions or angle marks.
spec.answerVisibility: All figure elements are permanent givens.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In $\triangle EBA$, $\angle EAB$ is a right angle and $\angle BEA=30^\circ$. If $EB=40\text{ m}$, use trigonometry to show that the height of the mast $AB$ is $20\text{ m}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: In $\triangle EBA$, use Pythagoras’ theorem to find the length $EA$, giving your answer in simplest surd form.

children.label: c
children.prompt: In $\triangle CBA$, $\angle CAB$ is a right angle and the length $AC$ is $11.547\text{ m}$. Find the size of $\angle BCA$, giving your answer correct to the nearest degree.

children.label: d
children.prompt: In $\triangle DBA$, $\angle DAB$ is a right angle and $\angle BDA=40^\circ$. Calculate the length $AD$, giving your answer as a number of metres correct to 3 decimal places.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Calculate the combined distance $(EA+CA+DA)$, giving your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Retain the unrounded value of $DA$.

$$\begin{align*}EA+CA+DA&=20\sqrt3+11.547+\frac{20}{\tan40^\circ}\\EA+CA+DA&\approx70.02\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
